what: The pause menu's eight sounds, rendered offline with the same recipes and reverb the game uses (features/game/audio/ui-sounds.ts), at the game's default master volume (0.6), and measured (features/game/debug/audio-analysis.ts). Read in the browser with window.__catopia.reportUiSounds().
brief: Short, soft, tactile electronic UI sounds for a premium pause menu: muted digital clicks, delicate synth blips, subtle airy textures, tiny mechanical ticks and smooth tonal transitions; crisp but not sharp, futuristic but not overly sci-fi, satisfying depth with a very short reverb; no harsh beeps, loud impacts or conventional mouse clicks.
how: Each sound is a small recipe of layers: a tiny band-passed-noise tick, a soft low pulse, rounded sine or triangle notes with a faint octave, and an airy filtered-noise sweep, plus a generated 0.28 s reverb. 44.1 kHz, both channels averaged for the measurement.

columns.peakDb: loudest moment, in decibels below full scale (0 would be the loudest a speaker can play)
columns.rmsDb: average loudness over the audible part
columns.audibleMs: time from the first to the last moment louder than -50 dB
columns.centroidHz: centre of the spectrum: low is soft and dark, high is sharp and bright

sounds.name: move
sounds.when: the highlight moves to another row (pitch climbs a gentle scale down the menu)

sounds.name: adjust
sounds.when: a choice steps forward or back (two notes, rising or falling)

sounds.name: select
sounds.when: pressing Begin (a rising pair with a breath of air)

sounds.name: toggleOn
sounds.when: a switch goes on (Sound, Performance numbers)

reading: Every sound is under a fifth of a second audible, peaks between 14.5 and 19.4 dB below full scale (soft, with no loud impacts), and none clips. The spectrum centres sit between 554 and 1559 Hz: warm and rounded, nowhere near the 3 kHz and above of a harsh beep. Before the menu level was raised by 6 dB the same sounds peaked 20.5 to 25.5 dB below full scale, which was too quiet to hear comfortably on small speakers.
notDone: These are measurements, not a listening test. Whether the sounds feel right (soft enough, bright enough, the right amount of reverb, the right notes) is for the owner's ears.
